Lazy stdlib loader.

Every std/<name> module except system, json and strings can be built as libdfkup_<name>.dylib and is loaded on the first import "std/<name>". Scripts that import nothing pay nothing. The three exceptions live in lang/lowlibs and are always linked into the host binary (CLI and node addon alike), so they never touch a dylib.

Dylib entry points mirror pluginkit's low-level conventions (C ABI, no plugin DSL):

  • dfkupStdlibAbi(): uint32 must equal dfkupStdlibAbiVersion
  • dfkupStdlibNim(): cstring must equal the host NimVersion
  • dfkupStdlibInit(script, sysmod, outModule, outErr): cint
  • optional dfkupStdlibCleanup() run from cleanupStdlibs
  • optional dfkupStdlibSetVm(vm) giving the dylib the host VM (libhttp: server callbacks re-enter the VM through the JIT bridge, whose jitGlobalVm lives per-image; the ABI version is unchanged since every addition is nil-tolerant)

Handles are never unloaded; the CLI runs once per process.

lowlibs/libjson, lowlibs/libstrings, lowlibs/libsequtils, lowlibs/libregex

Every stdlib name import "std/<name>" resolves. system, json and strings are served from lang/lowlibs in-image; the rest load from dylib shards (CLI) or the static bundle (napibuild).

proc cleanupStdlibs() {....raises: [Exception], tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}
Run optional per-stdlib cleanup hooks (e.g. reap headless browsers). Never unloads: the CLI runs once per process. 
proc clearActiveConfig() {....raises: [StdlibLoadError, Exception],
                           tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}
Clear the std/config declaration retained by the config dylib. No-op when the dylib is not loaded yet (there is no state to clear); runConfigFile calls this both before (unloaded) and after (loaded). 
proc configLibHandle(): LibHandle {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Handle of the loaded config dylib, or nil when not loaded yet. 
proc dfkupHostRaise(msg: cstring) {.cdecl, ...raises: [ValueError], tags: [],
                                    forbids: [].}
Host error sink installed into every shard before its init. A shard foreign proc that raises is caught in-image by its guard wrapper and re-raised here, so the exception is host-native and catchable as usual (message intact). Raising directly from dylib code would miss every host handler — each image owns its handler chain — and kill the process. 
proc findConfigCommand(cfg: pointer; name: string): string {.
    ...raises: [StdlibLoadError, Exception, ValueError], tags: [RootEffect],
    forbids: [].}
Look up one command in a retained config value across the dylib boundary. Raises ValueError (like the static helper did) on unknown commands or malformed declarations. 
proc hasStdlibLib(name: string): bool {....raises: [], tags: [ReadEnvEffect,
    ReadIOEffect, ReadDirEffect], forbids: [].}
True when a dylib file exists for name (no loading attempted). Under napibuild the libs are statically linked, so every known name is available without probing the filesystem. 
proc loadStdlibFactory(name: string): ModuleLibrary {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Vancode StdlibLoader entry: nil when name is not a known dfkup stdlib (vancode reports ErrImportError); otherwise a caching factory that loads on first use. Load/init failures raise StdlibLoadError, which vancode reports with file/line context. 
proc loadStdlibModule(name: string; script: Script; sysmod: Module): Module {.
    ...raises: [KeyError, CodeGenError, ValueError, StdlibLoadError, Exception],
    tags: [ReadEnvEffect, ReadIOEffect, ReadDirEffect, RootEffect], forbids: [].}

Build the populated Module for std/<name>. Raises StdlibLoadError.

json, strings, sequtils and regex are owned by dfkup (lang/lowlibs) and always served in-image, in both CLI and addon builds: no dlopen, no ABI or Nim version checks (one compiler by construction), no retains or slot reservations (same heap), no raise-sink (native exceptions). Every other stdlib dlopens its libdfkup_<name>.dylib (CLI) or builds from the static bundle (napibuild, see lowlibs/liball).

proc setStdlibVms(vm: pointer) {....raises: [Exception], tags: [RootEffect],
                                 forbids: [].}
Push the host VM into every loaded dylib that asked for it (dfkupStdlibSetVm export). Runs once the VM exists, before interpret: stdlib factories load at compile time, when no VM exists yet, so the handoff cannot happen in loadStdlibModule. 
proc stdlibDynlibLoaded(): bool {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
True once any stdlib dylib was initialized this process. The host uses it to decide whether compiler state must be retained (below). 
proc stdlibLibExt(): string {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Platform shard extension. Must match what tools/build_shards.nim in the stdkups repo emits (.dylib macOS, .dll Windows, .so elsewhere) so release archives bundle loadable shards per target. 
proc stdlibLibPath(name: string): string {....raises: [],
    tags: [ReadEnvEffect, ReadIOEffect, ReadDirEffect], forbids: [].}
Filesystem path of the libdfkup_<name> shard, "" when absent. ~/.dfkup/libraries is the package-manager-owned shared-library dir (DFKUP_HOME overrides the home) — release archives ship a libraries/ dir for exactly this spot. Next to the binary are the dev fallback (the shard build script writes bin/stdlib/ there) and the extracted-archive layout (libraries/ beside the binary). 
proc takeActiveConfig(): pointer {....raises: [StdlibLoadError, Exception],
                                   tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}
Peek at the retained config value as an opaque pointer. The dylib keeps its global reference alive (a raw pointer carries no ARC ownership); the caller releases via clearActiveConfig. Nil when no declaration ran.
